From the machine

Editor's Letter

Seven pieces out this July. Baseball Cap in Ditto Chord corduroy, 1h, 1/5. Cap sleeve shirt in Japanese cotton, size M, 2h, 4/5. Box Pleated Skirt in Beglarian Wool, 2h, 4/5, waist roomy. Pleated Trousers in the same wool, size 31, 4h, worn once, 4/5. Henley in waffle, size C, 3h, 3/5. Trigg Shorts in waffle, size C, 2h, 4/5. Curve Jacket in white twill and Japanese print cotton, size S modified, 3h, 5/5.

Every piece scored difficulty 1/5. You logged 68 finished for the year against 19 same month last year, and this July ran fast and easy across the board. The Skirt sits at 4/5 in a category averaging 3.7 across eight makes, your lowest-rated category and your least practised. Two hours matches the Skirt average. Trousers still cost you 5.2h on average and you cleared these in 4h. The pattern here is speed with no drop in rating. The Cap alone broke it at 1/5, your worst ever, and it took the least time.

The Cap sleeve shirt reads cropped and boxy with a stand collar. Wear it over the Pleated Bermuda Shorts in Japanese fabric. Matte black shirt against black shorts, both wide through the hip, the cropped hem stopping at the shorts waistband. For the Box Pleated Skirt, the waist runs roomy, so belt it or size the tuck. Pair it with the Boatneck Shirt in Japanese cotton tucked in. Both black, both structured, the skirt pleats holding volume the shirt keeps flat.

— M
